item.title: Musk and Zuckerberg echo Trump's push to rebrand AI as 'super intelligence' on earnings calls. Others do not
item.description:
- Last month, Trump ordered that “super intelligence” replace the term artificial intelligence within the government.
A month after [President Donald Trump](https://www.cnbc.com/donald-trump/) [ordered](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/29/trump-ai-super-intelligence.html) that “super intelligence” replace the term artificial intelligence within executive branch departments and agencies, his leading tech allies, [Elon Musk](https://www.cnbc.com/elon-musk/) and [Mark Zuckerberg](https://www.cnbc.com/mark-zuckerberg/), followed suit on earnings calls.
The president this week announced on Truth Social that he’s [banning](https://www.forbes.com/sites/fionariley/2026/10/27/trump-vows-to-ban-term-artificial-intelligence/) the use of the terms “AI” and “artificial intelligence” in “all relevant documents” and “everything else.”

item.title: Report from the Vatican
item.description:
# Report from the Vatican ### Yesterday I had the singular honor of meeting His Holiness, Pope Leo XIV _“So-called artificial intelligences do not undergo experiences, do not possess a body, do not feel joy or pain, do not mature through relationships and do not know from within what love, work, friendship or responsibility mean” ( **[no. 99](https://www.vatican.va/content/leo-xiv/en/encyclicals/documents/20260515-magnifica-humanitas.html)**)._
_For this reason, artificial intelligence must be “disarmed” ( **[no. 110](https://www.vatican.va/content/leo-xiv/en/encyclicals/documents/20260515-magnifica-humanitas.html)**), and I encourage the States meeting in Geneva in November to take concrete steps toward banning lethal autonomous weapons._

item.title: How Much AI Is Too Much AI In Campaign Ads?
item.description:
## What’sAt Stake?Everything. That’s how Travis Ridout, co-director of the [Wesleyan Media Project](https://mediaproject.wesleyan.edu/releases-101526/), sees the 2026 midterms, the first in which campaigns have truly embraced artificial intelligence.
He cites using AI to enhance existing content, specifically removing a buzzer sound interrupting a candidate while making a clip-worthy statement at a debate.
Four states — California, Maryland, Minnesota and Texas — have [laws](https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/artificial-intelligence-ai-in-elections-and-campaigns) that prohibit certain uses or types of AI-generated deepfakes in political messaging, and 27 states insist on some form of disclosure.
